name: Entity Graph
blurb: Every company, model, paper, person, dataset, benchmark, and regulation as a node.

reading.body:
The graph contains 23,034 nodes as of August 2026, and the single largest category by count is not models, companies, or research papers but state AI bills at 2,740, which outnumbers every technical node type.

Open models account for 15,247 of those nodes, making them the dominant technical mass in the graph. By contrast, the datasets that trained or evaluated those models number only 17, and the benchmarks used to assess them number only 18. The ratio is not a quirk of coverage choices; it reflects a real asymmetry in the ecosystem, where model proliferation has far outpaced the shared infrastructure of evaluation and data curation. Hardware entries stand at 37, a category the site treats as a curated and verified set, which means the physical layer underlying all 15,247 open models is represented by fewer than 40 distinct entries.

The legislative count, 2,740 state bills tracked against 269 companies and 64 named people, points to regulatory surface area expanding faster than the institutional actors it targets. What the data does not cover is the relationship between nodes: how many of the 1,803 papers cited by tracked models connect to the 134 editorially tracked papers, which companies built which models, or which hardware entries constrain which model families. The graph's shape is declared but its edges are not exposed here, so the node counts describe the vocabulary of the ecosystem without yet describing its grammar.
